title: People-centred leadership: the competitive advantage that will determine success in the age of artificial intelligence
summary: Discover why people-centred leadership is essential in the age of artificial intelligence and how it drives innovation, talent management, business transformation and sustainable growth.
body_markdown:
## Human leadership is becoming a strategic factor in the age of AI


In a context shaped by digital transformation and the rise of artificial intelligence, people-centred leadership is establishing itself as a key factor for business success. Organisations that prioritise talent management, trust and the development of their teams not only improve their competitiveness, but also strengthen their ability to adapt to change.


Companies across various sectors are embracing leadership models that place people at the heart of transformation. Reskilling and upskilling programmes linked to artificial intelligence are demonstrating that the adoption of technology is far more effective when combined with human support, continuous learning and open communication.


Similarly, organisations that have fostered cultures of continuous feedback and active listening have succeeded in improving the working environment, driving innovation and increasing their teams’ engagement.


## Why people-centred leadership is more important today than ever before


People-centred leadership means creating a space where people feel seen, valued, supported and empowered to give their best. It is about recognising strengths, nurturing potential and giving teams the confidence they need to grow.


In today’s world, characterised by rapid change and artificial intelligence, this type of leadership becomes the human anchor of organisations. It provides guidance, builds the trust needed to explore new tools and new ways of working, and inspires teams to move towards the future with curiosity and confidence.


People-centred leadership transforms uncertainty into opportunity and potential into progress.


## How to develop talent and accelerate team growth


Leaders who believe in growth are able to identify each person’s unique talent.


They listen actively, understand individual motivations, recognise strengths and create opportunities for people to realise their full potential. They also help professionals take on responsibilities and roles where they can truly add value and grow.


When this happens, professional development ceases to be an individual process and becomes a shared journey where each person’s success contributes to the growth of the organisation as a whole.


## Business transformation works best when people feel supported


Transformation strategies are more likely to succeed when people feel supported, valued and connected to the purpose of the change.


A people-centred leader helps to explain the rationale behind the transformation, listens to concerns with empathy and provides stability in times of uncertainty.


When there is clarity, trust and open communication, teams find the motivation they need to tackle new challenges and turn change into an opportunity for growth.


In this context, digital transformation does not depend solely on technology. It also depends on leaders’ ability to mobilise talent, build trust and support people throughout the process.


## Active listening and empathy: the skills that set the best leaders apart


Active listening and empathy lie at the heart of people-centred leadership.


These skills enable a better understanding of each professional’s needs, strengths and expectations, facilitating more balanced and effective decision-making.


When people feel heard and respected, their commitment, level of engagement and willingness to contribute to collective success increase, even in complex or highly uncertain situations.


For this reason, people skills are becoming increasingly valuable in an environment where technical skills can be complemented by artificial intelligence tools.


## Trust and collaboration as drivers of innovation and learning


Organisational cultures based on trust, continuous learning and collaboration do not arise spontaneously.


They are built when leaders create safe spaces for dialogue, listen to their teams’ concerns and encourage the sharing of different viewpoints, including critical or dissenting opinions.


Even when there are external constraints that cannot be changed immediately, leaders can work alongside their teams to identify areas for improvement and drive changes that lie within their sphere of influence.


This approach fosters continuous learning, strengthens team cohesion and creates more innovative and resilient environments.


## People-centred leadership drives sustainable growth and adaptation to change


People-centred leadership drives sustainable growth because it unlocks the full potential of teams.


When people feel supported, motivated and valued, they contribute creativity, accountability and the capacity for innovation. These factors are essential for tackling current challenges and responding agilely to new opportunities.


In times of transformation, strong leadership provides stability and inspires teams to learn, adapt and explore new possibilities, including the integration of artificial intelligence into day-to-day activities.


A mindset based on openness, curiosity and continuous improvement enables the building of more resilient organisations, prepared to face changing scenarios and compete successfully in the long term.


Sustainable success is achieved when people have the resources, trust and autonomy needed to become the best version of themselves.


## The future of leadership in the age of artificial intelligence


Artificial intelligence will continue to transform the way we work, learn and collaborate. However, human leadership will continue to play an essential role.


Organisations will need leaders capable of combining technology with deeply human skills such as empathy, curiosity, active listening, emotional intelligence, ethical judgement and the ability to build trust.


In an increasingly automated world, these skills will make the difference between managing processes and leading people.


Companies that manage to strike a balance between technological innovation and human leadership will be better placed to drive growth, nurture talent and successfully tackle the challenges of the future.


## Telefónica and people-centred leadership in the digital transformation


People-centred leadership aligns directly with Telefónica’s vision of driving a digital transformation that is responsible, sustainable and focused on talent development.


This is because the adoption of new technologies does not depend solely on the tools available, but also on organisations’ ability to prepare people, develop new skills and build trust throughout the process of change.


In this context, Telefónica is working to enable businesses, public authorities and citizens to access the most advanced digital technologies in a simple, secure and scalable way, whilst fostering a culture based on continuous learning, innovation and professional development.


As part of this vision, Telefónica has taken on the challenge of **“becoming the best gateway for citizens to digital technologies”** and of offering **“the best network for accessing the most innovative technology”** , convinced that true technological progress is only possible when people are at the heart of the transformation.
